projects.name: SS Security Co
projects.summary: A Manchester security firm that avoided padlock clichés. The doubled SS mark balances straight lines for strength with curves for approachability.

sections.heading: Who they are
sections.body: SS Security Co is a Manchester-based startup providing physical security services to nationwide corporate clients and residential buildings. As a new company, they came to us with no previous branding in place.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: SS Security Co were already experts in their field, but without branding nothing communicated that expertise. The security industry is full of predictable visual shorthand, like padlocks and shields, and they didn't want to blend in. The brand had to carry the same authority as the service.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body: We built the identity around strength, approachability, simplicity, legibility, professionalism, and national reach. The first concept paired two S's at odds with each other and read as busy rather than confident. The approved direction was a doubled SS where straight lines and curves work together, giving the mark both structure and warmth.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: The final mark combines two S's built from straight lines and curves. The repetition improves legibility at a glance, whether it's stamped small on a laptop or embroidered large on a jacket. The palette is a deep blue toned toward purple for trust. The system was applied across business cards, laptop decals and uniform embroidery, with clear logo construction and clear-space guidelines.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: For the first time, SS Security Co's branding and expertise work hand in hand. The visual identity now carries the same authority the company already had in the industry.

projects.name: Coffee By The Corner
projects.summary: A cosy independent coffee shop whose cold, plain branding was replaced with warm browns, terracotta and cream. The logo's sharp corner nods to the name.

sections.heading: Who they are
sections.body: Coffee By The Corner is a small independent coffee shop serving coffee, breakfast, lunch and snacks, and occasionally hosting local events. Warm, cosy and full of character, it feels like a home away from home.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: The existing branding told a different story: a plain font on a white background, stark, cold and clinical. It was the opposite of what the shop feels like inside. The brand should have delivered that warmth before you even walked in.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body: The interior became the brief. Cosy corners, considered spaces and a sense of belonging were strategic details, so the direction was to build an identity that earns the warmth the shop already delivers.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: The logo mark is a rectangle with two rounded corners and two sharp ones, a deliberate nod to the name. A warm palette of deep browns, terracotta and cream replaces the cold white. The result is calm, grounded and inviting.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: The new brand matches the shop it represents. It communicates warmth, friendliness and community the moment someone encounters it.

projects.name: Better UK
projects.summary: A community health and wellbeing organisation across the UK. A shield, interlocking lines and a central figure express safety, connection and inclusion.

sections.heading: Who they are
sections.body: Better UK is a community-first organisation operating across the United Kingdom, helping people of all ages lead healthier, more active lives through accessible facilities, programmes and initiatives.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: Better UK had many facilities and an inclusive approach, but their branding didn't communicate it. The identity felt outdated, inconsistent and scattered, so members couldn't instantly see what the brand stood for.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body: We started with the core values at the heart of Better UK: community, accessibility, health and wellbeing, positivity and reliability. These values guided every design decision.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: The logo has three elements. The shield signals safety and reliability. Two overlapping lines inside it symbolise connection and unity. A simplified figure at the centre represents the people at the heart of the brand. Clean, legible typography and balanced layouts keep the identity energetic yet approachable.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: Better UK now has a clear, unified presence across digital and physical platforms. Audiences immediately understand the brand stands for community, wellbeing and positive change.

projects.name: Mevo Banking
projects.summary: A fintech built on speed and trust. Two flowing waves form an M, pairing fluid movement with deep blues for stability.

sections.heading: Intro
sections.body: Mevo makes banking simple and reliable. Their fintech product was fast and dependable, but their branding didn't say so. They wanted a brand that reflected speed, clarity, trust and simplicity.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: The brief was tricky. Early ideas blended into the competition, Monzo, Revolut and Starling, and nothing felt original. Mevo needed a brand with meaning that connected with risk-takers, small business owners and anyone who values simple, fast banking.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body: A strategy session uncovered four values: simplicity, reliability, progress and connection. These principles guided every design decision.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: Inspiration came from movement: money moves, people move, businesses move, and waves move. That became two waves forming an M. The visual identity pairs fluid forms with structured layouts and deep blues for stability and trust. The tone is calm yet confident, fast yet dependable.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: Mevo's new brand reflects who they really are, a fintech that moves with its customers: fast, trustworthy and human. It resonates with risk-takers, doers and small business owners, and sets Mevo apart in a crowded market.

projects.name: Royal Advisors
projects.summary: A business consultancy for founders. A custom R mark, emerald, gold and royal purple palette, and the slogan Launch. Grow. Succeed.

sections.heading: Who they are
sections.body: Royal Advisors is a business consulting firm built for founders who want more than generic advice, from setting up a first company to scaling an existing one. Their ethos is that they care about your business as much as you do.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: Business consulting is a crowded, corporate space of cold blues and stiff layouts. Royal Advisors needed an identity that felt modern and confident without looking like every other consultancy, and they needed it in two weeks.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body: A full brand strategy workshop produced three values: honest, clear and precise. Honest means telling clients what they need to hear. Clear means no jargon. Precise means every recommendation is built for the client, never off the shelf.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: The identity is built around a custom geometric R mark. The palette moves away from corporate blues to emerald, rich gold, royal purple and ivory. A gradient-free system carries the brand, typeset in Man Rope. The project delivered three logo variants, a full palette, brand guidelines and a tone of voice. The slogan, Launch. Grow. Succeed., ties it together.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: The identity matches who Royal Advisors are and the client was thrilled. The project expanded into a full brand guidelines system and a website, built in four hours on top of the two-week brand delivery.

projects.name: Veloria Home
projects.summary: A homeware brand turning everyday essentials into comfort. A house outline frames a V and a pillow icon, set in gold, pine green and sage.

sections.heading: Who they are
sections.body: Veloria Home offers stylish, practical homeware designed to make every space feel calm, cosy and welcoming, from bedding and pillows to towels and accessories.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: The existing identity was a plain black-and-white logo on a shopping bag. It lacked personality and any connection to the home. Veloria Home needed a brand that communicated comfort, quality and approachability in a competitive market.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body: Four values shaped the work: warmth and comfort, modern elegance, thoughtful quality and elevated simplicity. They guided every visual, typographic and tonal decision.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: The logo pairs a simplified home outline with a subtle V cut into a rounded triangle. At the centre, a pillow icon doubles as a top-down bed. Typography blends approachability with clarity. The palette is gold for warmth, pine green and sage for balance, and off-white as a clean base.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: Veloria Home's brand moved from lifeless to engaging. The house-shaped logo places the business clearly in home retail, and the tone of voice is warm, clear and confident.

projects.name: PinkLime
projects.summary: A Manchester web design agency given a full redesign. The signature pink stays, and the lime becomes a playful, modern mark with a cursor.

sections.heading: Who they are
sections.body: PinkLime is a Manchester, women-led web design agency serving small businesses and startups, helping them build websites that feel credible, modern and human.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: Even good designers can fall into the trap of not fixing their own work. Small tweaks over time had made PinkLime's logo lower in quality, and their website and visuals didn't show the professionalism of their work.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body: Keep the signature pink to preserve recognition, show personality with a playful but professional logo, signal credibility, and highlight the USP: serious but not corporate, human but not soft.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: A complete brand redesign. The logo is a lime with a slice replaced by a cursor, rounded, calm, modern and playful. The colours, typography and graphics were updated to match the brand's personality.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: The redesign immediately elevated PinkLime's credibility. Clients now see a professional, playful and human agency, and the perception shift alone makes them more trustworthy and premium.

projects.name: Rapid Transit
projects.summary: Premium ride-hailing for business travel, sitting between taxis and chauffeurs. An R and T merge with an arrow, in neon green and dark tones.

sections.heading: Who they are
sections.body: Rapid Transit is a premium ride-hailing service for business professionals. It sits between traditional taxis and executive chauffeur services, offering speed without sacrificing comfort.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: Competitors lean either cheap and fast, or premium and slow. Rapid Transit needed to sit in a different lane: fast, precise and high-end, without feeling like just another Uber-style service.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body: The brand is built on three principles: speed, efficiency and luxury. Everything had to communicate movement and control rather than chaos.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.body: The logo merges an R and a T into a clean, structured mark, with an arrow at the centre of the R for forward motion and precision. Neon green reflects energy and pace, balanced with darker, refined tones for a feeling that is quick but never rushed, and premium but never slow.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: Rapid Transit stands apart as a service built for people who move differently, delivering fast, efficient travel with a considered, high-end quality.
